chunk_findings.detail: `_gate_outcome` computes the gate outcome from only `best.findings`, while the caller still chooses `best = min(results, key=lambda r: r.status)`. On a converged full re-review with two `RV.REVIEWED` results, if the first result contains only below-floor findings (e.g. one `LOW`) and the second result contains a `HIGH` finding, `RV.blocking_findings(best.findings, converged=True, floor="HIGH")` returns empty and `_gate_outcome` returns `"passed"`, silently ignoring the other reviewer’s `HIGH` finding. Before this change, the first result’s `LOW` finding made `best.findings` truthy and the gate failed; the new convergence rule turns that previously failing state into a false pass whenever the first status-minimal result is non-blocking. The convergence decision must aggregate blocking findings across all reviewed results, not only the first status-minimal one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_gate_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to prove that the HIGH convergence floor is not a free pass, but its second review call is `_review(repo)` without `full=True`. The file’s own convergence comment says a delta or fix round blocks at any severity, so this assertion can pass even when the convergence/full path is broken: for example, if `blocking_findings` used `>` instead of `>=` against the floor, a full converged round would incorrectly pass a new HIGH finding, while this non-full delta/fix review would still block for the unrelated reason that delta/fix rounds block everything. Thus the test does not actually guard the claimed “new HIGH in a converged later round still blocks” behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The new pooling of findings only happens when `converged_round` is true; the conservative `else best.findings` branch preserves the same ignored-finding bug on the non-converged path. With two `RV.REVIEWED` results where `best` (the first result when statuses tie under `min(results, key=lambda r: r.status)`) has no findings and the second `RV.REVIEWED` result has a `HIGH` finding, `found` is `best.findings` (empty), so the `if not found` branch returns `"passed"` before the second reviewer’s `HIGH` is ever examined. A normal non-converged review can therefore pass despite a HIGH finding.

chunk_findings.detail: `_floor_for` returns `cfg.review.converge_floor` for every `kind == "full"` and `not fix`, with no check for a prior round. The call site in `_record_review` passes it unconditionally, so the convergence-floor paragraph is sent on the first full review of a change (`kind="full"`, `fix=False`, no prior review). On that first review the paragraph tells the reviewer not to report a new MEDIUM/LOW finding against unchanged context lines, even though there was no earlier round; such a finding has not been seen before and should block. The `_gate_outcome` path guards with `_rounds_used(it, gate) > 0`, but the prompt path does not, contradicting the `_converges` docstring (“a full, non-fix re-review only”). This can cause an initial review to pass despite a real below-floor defect on never-reviewed context lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_floor_for

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test changes the only reviewed file before the later round: `_fix(repo)` rewrites `x.py` to `x = 2  # the defect is fixed`, while the later fake reviewer emits its new MEDIUM finding at `x.py:1`. Since `x.py` was changed since the last review, the finding is not "against a file unchanged since the last review" as the convergence rule in the module docstring requires; under that rule it should still block. The assertion `later.data["outcome"] == "passed"` is therefore wrong for this input, and the test would either fail against a correct implementation that checks the unchanged-file condition or would only pass because the implementation ignores below-floor findings on newly fixed files.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_gate_outcome` helper is added but never called in the production path. The only changed call site in this file is the `_with_previous_findings` lambda; `_record_review` (which turns review results into the gate outcome/evidence) is not modified to use the helper. Therefore a full re-review whose only current findings are below `converge_floor` still cannot be marked passed by this logic: e.g. with `converge_floor="HIGH"` and one MEDIUM finding in round 2, `_record_review` will use the old outcome computation and keep the gate failed, so the convergence fix is not actually in effect (any passing regression test must be calling the helper directly).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_gate_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: `converged_round` is true whenever `converging` and `_rounds_used(it, gate) > 0`, without requiring that the prior round was a full reviewed round or produced findings. A recorded unavailable/error round consumes a review round, so after round 1 is unavailable and round 2 is the first successful full review, `_rounds_used` is 1 and the floor is applied. With `converge_floor="HIGH"`, a MEDIUM finding from that first substantive review is treated as converged and the gate passes, even though there was no previous full review for the author to converge against and the prompt may not have suppressed the finding. The convergence floor should require a prior full review (or prior findings) rather than any used round.

The only new call site in this diff is the `_with_previous_findings(..., floor=_floor_for(...))` lambda, which only changes the reviewer prompt; `_record_review` is not modified to use `_gate_outcome` or `RV.blocking_findings`. chunk_findings.detail: With `converge_floor="HIGH"`, a first full review that records a MEDIUM finding fails because `converged_round` is false. If the author does not fix that MEDIUM and a later full re-review repeats the same MEDIUM finding, `_gate_outcome` sees the previous round’s non-empty `chunk_findings`, sets `converged_round=True`, and calls `RV.blocking_findings` with only the current findings and the floor. Because the repeated MEDIUM is below `HIGH`, it is filtered out and `_gate_outcome` returns `"passed"` with a `converged` flag. This lets an unresolved MEDIUM that was blocking in the prior round pass without a fix, contradicting the function’s stated rule that only a *new* below-floor nit should not re-open the gate and the prompt’s instruction to report a same defect that still stands.
